subject: Proposal: phased consumption migration + temporary price collar
messages:
From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@nebula.ai>
Cc: Priya Desai <priya@nebula.ai>
Date: Tue, 7 Dec 2027 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: Proposal: phased consumption migration + temporary price collar

Hi Sanjay / Priya,

Thanks again for the time last week. Nebula's usage profile shows a clear shift toward bursty inference across Q3–Q4; we think a two-step migration from your current retainer to a consumption-first model will lower unit cost while preserving predictability during the transition.

Attached is an initial term sheet (NEB-term-sheet-v2.pdf) and the usage export we reviewed. High-level proposal:
- Phase 1 (3 months): "stability window" with a temporary price collar — your effective per-token rate will be sheltered within a +/- 10% band versus current blended rate to avoid immediate volatility.
- Phase 2 (6 months): gradual consumption ramp with milestone true-ups and a one-time migration allowance applied as credit on first invoice.
- Protection: automatic rollback to a capped retainer rate if sustained monthly spend drops below a pre-agreed floor.

Questions for you:
1) Would Nebula accept a 3-month collar period as described?
2) Any regulatory or procurement constraints we should model in the term sheet (SAML, audit logs retention)?
3) Suggested owners on your side for migration milestones and acceptance criteria?

Proposed next step: 30-minute alignment call Thursday 12/9 10:00am PT — I can share a mutual action plan (MAP) during the call.

Regards,
David
David Kim
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: Nebula_usage_report_Q3.xlsx (xlsx)]

From: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@nebula.ai>
To: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Desai <priya@nebula.ai>
Date: Tue, 7 Dec 2027 11:02:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Proposal: phased consumption migration + temporary price collar

David —

Thanks for the write-up and the export. This direction makes sense given our Q3 burst patterns. A couple of items from Finance & Ops:
- Finance would prefer a minimum revenue floor for the 6-month window; can you include a monthly floor in the term sheet?
- Legal will need to review any rollback/rollback-trigger language; please send the full term PDF.
- We need clarity on how the migration allowance posts on invoices (credit vs. negative line item).

I can attend the 12/9 call. Priya will be on procurement/legal review and will share redline comments after the call. Owners on our side: Priya (legal/procurement) and me (platform lead).

—Sanjay
Sanjay Rao
Head of Engineering, Nebula AI
[sanjay@nebula.ai]

From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@nebula.ai>
Cc: Priya Desai <priya@nebula.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 8 Dec 2027 08:23:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Proposal: phased consumption migration + temporary price collar

Sanjay —

Thanks — attaching NEB-term-sheet-v2.pdf with the explicit monthly floor and a short example invoice mockup. Key clarifications we added:
- Monthly floor: $65k/mo for the 6-month migration window; if monthly invoiced usage falls below the floor, the difference will be invoiced but eligible for a 1x make-good credit delivered at migration completion.
- Migration allowance: one-time credit applied as a line item on month 1 of Phase 2; we label it "Migration Allowance" so your accounting team can reconcile easily.
- Collar mechanics: +/-10% versus current blended per-token effective rate; collar protects Nebula from short-term spikes.

Quick ask for the call: Priya, if possible bring a short list of mandatory legal edits so we can triage. Karthik, can you confirm whether the proposed collar interacts cleanly with the dynamic batching incentive in our runtime (we want to avoid double-counting discounts)?

Call and MAP: I’ll send a calendar invite for 12/9 10am PT and populate the MAP with milestones and acceptance criteria.

Regards,
David
[Attachment: NEB-term-sheet-v2.pdf (pdf)]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 8 Dec 2027 09:10:00 -08:00
Subject: Fwd: Proposal: phased consumption migration + temporary price collar

Monica — forwarding the thread. We need CS playbook items to ensure Nebula hits the Phase 1 stability targets and to capture usage for the migration allowance.

Please review the term sheet attached and propose milestone acceptance criteria for the MAP (deployment test, 7-day stable throughput, billing reconciliation). I’ve asked Karthik to confirm pricing interactions.

Thanks — Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Director, Customer Success | Redwood Inference

From: Priya Desai <priya@nebula.ai>
To: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@nebula.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 9 Dec 2027 15:02:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Proposal: phased consumption migration + temporary price collar

David / all —

I reviewed NEB-term-sheet-v2.pdf and have a few redline items. In principle Nebula can accept a temporary collar and a phased migration, but we need the following edits before sign-off:
- Update clause 8b to replace an open-ended "rollback" term with a defined reversion procedure and a 30-day notice.
- Clarify that the migration allowance is a non-recurring credit for one billing period and not an ongoing discount.
- Include a data retention SLA reference to our SOC-2 scope (we will share the SOC-2 evidence list with you).

I attached a redline (NEB-term-sheet-v2-redline.docx). Once you return an updated PDF we can route to procurement. I can join the 12/9 10am PT call for legal alignment.

Best,
Priya Desai
Head of Procurement & Legal Operations, Nebula AI
[Attachment: NEB-term-sheet-v2-redline.docx (docx)]
